thread:
anya: Heads-up — onboarding the q4-ggml-8b quantized candidate into the eval harness. I spotted raw customer prompts in the CI artifact bundle. Need to gate this before we add it to nightly runs.
liam: oof. which job/artifact? can you paste the path?
anya: s3 path from the job: s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/2026-03-01/q4-ggml-8b/run-42/bundle.tgz — inside there is samples/prompts.txt with unredacted prompts.
marie: Ack. That's the new runner that mirrors local samples to artifacts for later human review. We forgot to wire the scrubbing hook.
liam: Repro steps I used: 
```bash
# from eval-runner container
ls /workspace/out || true
cat /workspace/out/samples/prompts.txt | head -n 10
```
showed clear PII.
sre-jen: We need a mitigation timeline. This is a data-exposure risk: artifact retention + ACLs could let non-owners see raw prompts. Priority: high.
anya: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) remove existing artifact bundle and rotate paths, 2) add a pre-upload scrubber that runs deterministic redaction, 3) change S3 ACLs so only eval-admins can access until cleared. Thoughts?
liam: Sounds right. Quick patch to runner: run scrubber if ENV ENABLE_PROMPT_SCRUB=true else fail the job. That gives us a hard stop while we patch upstream.
marie: Also add a CI check that prevents artifact upload if any line matches email/SSN regex or contains long numeric sequences. Small linter in the harness.
sre-jen: We should also ensure the scrubber is reproducible for evals (so we don't change distribution). Use a canonical token <REDACTED_PERSON> not anonymization with ids. Add a flag to keep mapping out of artifacts but store mapping only in KMS-protected vault if absolutely necessary.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: created chase-issue #4231 (evals: prompt artifact exposure) assigned to @liam, @anya, due 48h. :white_check_mark:
liam: I'll take the remove+rotate path now. Plan: remove s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/2026-03-01/q4-ggml-8b/run-42/bundle.tgz, rotate prefix to s3://redwood-evals/quarantined/1801238901-42/, tighten ACLs, and open PR for scrubber in the runner.
anya: I'll draft the scrubber PR. Key requirements: deterministic regex ruleset (emails, credit card patterns, phone numbers, long UUIDs), keep tokenization intact for metrics, and an integration test that asserts no blacklisted patterns remain.
marie: For integration test, add a small sample with edge cases (embedded code blocks, JSON prompts, base64 blobs) — these triggered misses in previous redactors. Also update the eval dashboard to flag any future model bring-up with a "artifact-scrubbed" badge.
liam: CI wiring: eval-ci needs a gating job that runs scrub-checker BEFORE archive step. If it fails, the job should fail and notify #eng-sre and the PR. I'll add a job in .github/workflows/eval-runner.yml.
marie: Metric/regression note: If we alter prompts (redaction replacing names), we should log that transformation but not include raw values in logs/artifacts. Add an audit record with metadata: job_id, scrub_rules_version, counts_of_replacements. Those audit records can be low-sensitivity and retained in internal DB with RBAC.
sre-jen: RBAC: eval artifacts bucket policy must deny GetObject unless request principal is in the eval-admins or the owning org role. Also add object tagging with sensitivity=pii when scrubber ran. That helps lifecycle policies.
anya: Quick question — do we want to run the scrubber client-side (in runner) or server-side (upload lambda)? Client-side is better for reducing egress of raw prompts, but needs to be in the runner image. Server-side lambda is easier to enforce centrally but still sees raw data.
liam: prefer client-side. We'll add the scrubber binary to the runner image and require Scrub=true in the job config. Server-side could be fallback for older runners.
marie: I'll draft the scrub rules doc and a small eval-harness test matrix. We should also schedule a 30-min sync with legal/security to confirm patterns and retention.
ops-bot: calendar-bot: meeting created "Eval artifact privacy sync" with legal/security on 2026-03-02 14:00 UTC.
anya: Assign next actions: liam — remove + ACLs + CI gating (24h), marie — scrub rules + integration tests (48h), me — runner scrubber PR + image build (48h).
liam: On it. I'll post a short postmortem once the artifact is rotated.
marie: Thanks all. Also adding a follow-up: tie artifact visibility to model onboarding checklist so no model reaches nightly without passing scrub checks.
sre-jen: Agree. After mitigation, run a quick org-wide audit for other pockets copying artifacts to public paths.
anya: Thanks — keeping this thread for updates. :lock:
